articles.headline: Will Lankshear scores brace as Middlesbrough come back to survive scare and beat Lincoln
articles.description: Marquee signing Will Lankshear notched a second-half double as Middlesbrough fought back to kick off their Championship bid with a hard-fought 2-1 victory and inflict a first defeat in eight and a half months on newly promoted Lincoln.

images.name: Will Lankshear [1296x729]
images.caption: Will Lankshear scored his first Championship goal for Middlesbrough to level the scores.

articles.headline: Nestory Irankunda leaves Watford for Portuguese giants Sporting CP
articles.description: Australia international Nestory Irankunda will feature in the UEFA Champions League this season after joining Portuguese giants Sporting CP.

images.caption: Nestory Irankunda, who became Australia's youngest scorer at a men's World Cup back in June, has joined Portuguese giants Sporting CP after one season in the Championship with Watford.

articles.headline: Raúl Jiménez marks Wolves return by rescuing draw with Blackburn

articles.headline: Dastan Satpayev signs Chelsea deal, joins Burnley on loan

seasonseries.title: Queens Park Rangers vs. Leicester City

keyEvents.text: First Half begins.
Goal! Queens Park Rangers 1, Leicester City 0. Koki Saito (Queens Park Rangers) header from the left side of the six yard box to the high centre of the goal. Assisted by Rumarn Burrell.
Goal! Queens Park Rangers 2, Leicester City 0. Richard Kone (Queens Park Rangers) left footed shot from the centre of the box to the high centre of the goal following a set piece situation.
Goal! Queens Park Rangers 3, Leicester City 0. Karamoko Dembélé (Queens Park Rangers) left footed shot from the centre of the box to the bottom right corner. Assisted by Rumarn Burrell.
Jordan Ayew (Leicester City) is shown the yellow card.

Goal! Queens Park Rangers 4, Leicester City 0. Amadou Mbengue (Queens Park Rangers) right footed shot from a difficult angle and long range on the right to the high centre of the goal. Assisted by Jimmy Dunne.
First Half ends, Queens Park Rangers 4, Leicester City 0.
Substitution, Queens Park Rangers. Steve Cook replaces Jake Clarke-Salter.
Second Half begins Queens Park Rangers 4, Leicester City 0.
Substitution, Leicester City. Hamza Choudhury replaces Jordan James.
Substitution, Leicester City. Silko-Amari Thomas replaces Jordan Ayew.
Substitution, Leicester City. Aaron Ramsey replaces Jannik Vestergaard.
Substitution, Leicester City. Jeremy Monga replaces Abdul Fatawu.
Substitution, Queens Park Rangers. Isaac Hayden replaces Jonathan Varane.
Substitution, Queens Park Rangers. Sam Field replaces Nicolas Madsen.
Ricardo Pereira (Leicester City) is shown the yellow card for a bad foul.
Penalty missed! Still Queens Park Rangers 4, Leicester City 0. Bobby De Cordova-Reid (Leicester City) hits the left post with a right footed shot.
Goal! Queens Park Rangers 4, Leicester City 1. Silko-Amari Thomas (Leicester City) left footed shot from the centre of the box to the centre of the goal following a set piece situation.
